verdict.rationale: Google Authenticator documentably generates TOTP codes (RFC 6238) for sites that support authenticator-app 2-Step Verification, and the app has a 'Scan QR code' action. However, the docs in this pack show that scan action only for transferring codes between devices. Adding a new account by scanning its setup QR code is implied only by community references to 'setup QR codes', and a 2013 report of crashes when scanning two QR codes in a row on iOS 7 is old and isolated. missing for 10: first-party documentation of the add-account flow from a service's setup QR code, evidence that codes appear immediately after scanning, current hands-on corroboration of new-account QR enrollment.

support.subject: As an everyday user, I can scan a QR code and immediately start generating TOTP codes for a new account

citations.quote: Time-based One-time Password (TOTP) algorithm specified in RFC 6238
The Google Authenticator app can generate one-time verification codes for sites and apps that support Authenticator app 2-Step Verification.
On your new device, tap Scan QR code
Workaround: screenshot every setup QR code and store the images safely for migration.
